Both diamond and graphite are made of the same element, carbon. However, the arrangement of these atoms in their structures gives them different properties and characteristics.

Diamond is a crystalline form of carbon in which each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement. This structure gives diamond its hardness and high melting point.

Graphite, on the other hand, is a form of carbon in which the carbon atoms are arranged in layers of hexagonal symmetry. These layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, which allows graphite to be soft and slippery.

So, while both diamond and graphite are made of carbon, the way they are arranged in their structures gives them different properties and characteristics.
